title: Zhou Yu Beats Huang Gai
synopsis: Zhou Yu arranges for Huang Gai to be viciously beaten, but it’s all part of a clever ruse.

series.title: Famous Sayings and Stories from the Three Kingdoms

fullText.simplified:
周瑜打黄盖——一个愿打，一个愿挨

    三国的时候，发生过不少有名的战争。其中，一场由大火开始的战争，改变了三国的历史。这是曹操与江东之间的战争。这场大火烧掉了曹操的战船，使曹操没能打过长江。
    这场大火是怎么烧起来的呢？这里面有个小故事。
    战争刚开始的时候，曹操的百万大军在长江北边，江东在长江南边，只有不到十万人。十万人当然不能和百万人打。江东的大将军周瑜想到了“火攻”——用大火烧掉曹操的战船。办法是好的，但江东要怎么去曹操的船队里放火呢？周瑜和江东另一位老将军黄盖一起想了个办法。他们决定进行一场“表演”。
    这场“表演”是从江东一个重要的会议开始的。在这个会议上，周瑜要求大家一起打曹操。黄盖故意站出来反对，说：“曹操有一百万人，我们才十万人，不能打！”周瑜假装很生气，让人重重地打了黄盖。黄盖是位老将军，这次被打得很重。他“生气地”写信给曹操，说要带着自己的人和战船来投降曹操。曹操收到信，高兴极了。
    在一个刮着东南风的晚上，黄盖带着战船，假装来投降曹操。当黄盖的战船靠近曹操的船队时，黄盖在战船上点了火，然后让着火的战船飞快地冲进曹操的船队。由于距离太近，而且风特别大，曹操来不及做任何事，只能看着自己的船队烧了起来。
    火越烧越大。同时，周瑜带着江东的大军出现在了江上。很快，曹操的大军被打败了。曹操这时候才明白，原来“周瑜打黄盖”是一场表演，目的是为了让曹操相信黄盖要来“投降”。这样，黄盖就能带着火船靠近曹操的船队了。
    后人从这个故事里总结了俗语：周瑜打黄盖——一个愿打，一个愿挨。它的意思是，两个人做一件事，虽然其中一个人要吃点苦头，但这是两个人都同意和接受的。
    生活中，人们也会说这句话。比如，弟弟的作业不会写，请姐姐帮忙。姐姐说：“我可以教你，但你要帮我打扫房间。”弟弟同意了。姐姐教弟弟完成了作业，弟弟花半天时间打扫了姐姐的房间，两个人都得到了自己需要的。这时候我们就可以说：“这姐弟俩是‘周瑜打黄盖——一个愿打，一个愿挨’。”
fullText.traditional:
周瑜打黃蓋——一個願打，一個願挨

    三國的時候，發生過不少有名的戰爭。其中，一場由大火開始的戰爭，改變了三國的歷史。這是曹操與江東之間的戰爭。這場大火燒掉了曹操的戰船，使曹操沒能打過長江。
    這場大火是怎麼燒起來的呢？這裡面有個小故事。
    戰爭剛開始的時候，曹操的百萬大軍在長江北邊，江東在長江南邊，只有不到十萬人。十萬人當然不能和百萬人打。江東的大將軍周瑜想到了“火攻”——用大火燒掉曹操的戰船。辦法是好的，但江東要怎麼去曹操的船隊裡放火呢？周瑜和江東另一位老將軍黃蓋一起想了個辦法。他們決定進行一場“表演”。
    這場“表演”是從江東一個重要的會議開始的。在這個會議上，周瑜要求大家一起打曹操。黃蓋故意站出來反對，說：“曹操有一百萬人，我們才十萬人，不能打！”周瑜假裝很生氣，讓人重重地打了黃蓋。黃蓋是位老將軍，這次被打得很重。他“生氣地”寫信給曹操，說要帶著自己的人和戰船來投降曹操。曹操收到信，高興極了。
    在一個颳著東南風的晚上，黃蓋帶著戰船，假裝來投降曹操。當黃蓋的戰船靠近曹操的船隊時，黃蓋在戰船上點了火，然後讓著火的戰船飛快地衝進曹操的船隊。由於距離太近，而且風特別大，曹操來不及做任何事，只能看著自己的船隊燒了起來。
    火越燒越大。同時，周瑜帶著江東的大軍出現在了江上。很快，曹操的大軍被打敗了。曹操這時候才明白，原來“周瑜打黃蓋”是一場表演，目的是為了讓曹操相信黃蓋要來“投降”。這樣，黃蓋就能帶著火船靠近曹操的船隊了。
    後人從這個故事裡總結了俗語：周瑜打黃蓋——一個願打，一個願挨。它的意思是，兩個人做一件事，雖然其中一個人要吃點苦頭，但這是兩個人都同意和接受的。
    生活中，人們也會說這句話。比如，弟弟的作業不會寫，請姐姐幫忙。姐姐說：“我可以教你，但你要幫我打掃房間。”弟弟同意了。姐姐教弟弟完成了作業，弟弟花半天時間打掃了姐姐的房間，兩個人都得到了自己需要的。這時候我們就可以說：“這姐弟倆是‘周瑜打黃蓋——一個願打，一個願挨’。”

sentences.english: This great fire burned Cao Cao’s warships, preventing him from crossing the Yangtze River.

sentences.english: How did this great fire start? There’s a little story behind it.

sentences.english: At the beginning of the war, Cao Cao’s army of one million men was on the north side of the Yangtze River.

sentences.pinyin: jiāng dōng zài cháng jiāng nán bian zhǐ yǒu bú dào shí wàn rén
sentences.english: Jiangdong was on the south side of the Yangtze River with fewer than one hundred thousand men.

sentences.simplified: 十万人当然不能和百万人打。
sentences.traditional: 十萬人當然不能和百萬人打。
sentences.pinyin: shí wàn rén dāng rán bù néng hé bǎi wàn rén dǎ
sentences.english: Of course, one hundred thousand men could not fight against one million men.

sentences.traditional: 江東的大將軍周瑜想到了“火攻”——用大火燒掉曹操的戰船。

sentences.english: The great general of Jiangdong, Zhou Yu, came up with the idea of a “fire attack”—using a great fire to burn Cao Cao’s warships.

sentences.english: This plan was good, but how was Jiangdong going to infiltrate Cao Cao’s fleet to start a fire?

sentences.simplified: 周瑜和江东另一位老将军黄盖一起想了个办法。
sentences.traditional: 周瑜和江東另一位老將軍黃蓋一起想了個辦法。

sentences.english: Zhou Yu and another veteran general from Jiangdong, Huang Gai, came up with a plan together.

sentences.traditional: 黃蓋故意站出來反對，說：“曹操有一百萬人，我們才十萬人，不能打！”

sentences.english: Huang Gai deliberately stood up to object, saying, “Cao Cao has a million men, while we have only a hundred thousand men. We can’t fight!”

sentences.english: Zhou Yu pretended to be very angry and ordered his men to give Huang Gai a severe beating.

sentences.english: Huang Gai was a veteran general, and this time he was badly beaten.

sentences.english: He “angrily” wrote a letter to Cao Cao, saying he would bring his men and warships to surrender to Cao Cao.

sentences.simplified: 曹操收到信，高兴极了。
sentences.traditional: 曹操收到信，高興極了。
sentences.pinyin: cáo cāo shōu dào xìn gāo xìng jí le
sentences.english: Cao Cao received this letter and was extremely happy.

sentences.english: On a night when the southeast wind was blowing, Huang Gai sailed with his warships, pretending to surrender to Cao Cao.

sentences.english: As Huang Gai’s ships approached Cao Cao’s fleet, he set them on fire and sent the burning warships rushing straight into Cao Cao’s fleet.

sentences.simplified: 弟弟同意了。
sentences.traditional: 弟弟同意了。
sentences.pinyin: dì di tóng yì le
sentences.english: The younger brother agrees.

sentences.simplified: 姐姐教弟弟完成了作业，
sentences.traditional: 姐姐教弟弟完成了作業，
sentences.pinyin: jiě jie jiāo dì di wán chéng le zuò yè
sentences.english: The older sister teaches her younger brother how to finish his homework, ..

sentences.simplified: 弟弟花半天时间打扫了姐姐的房间，
sentences.traditional: 弟弟花半天時間打掃了姐姐的房間，
sentences.pinyin: dì di huā bàn tiān shí jiān dǎ sǎo le jiě jie de fáng jiān
sentences.english: .. and the younger brother spends half a day cleaning his older sister’s room.

sentences.simplified: 两个人都得到了自己需要的。
sentences.traditional: 兩個人都得到了自己需要的。
sentences.pinyin: liǎng ge rén dōu dé dào le zì jǐ xū yào de
sentences.english: Both of them get what they wanted.

sentences.simplified: 这时候我们就可以说：“这姐弟俩是‘周瑜打黄盖——一个愿打，一个愿挨’。”
sentences.traditional: 這時候我們就可以說：“這姐弟倆是‘周瑜打黃蓋——一個願打，一個願挨’。”
sentences.pinyin: zhè shí hou wǒ men jiù kě yǐ shuō zhè jiě dì liǎ shì zhōu yú dǎ huáng gài yí ge yuàn dǎ yí ge yuàn ái
sentences.english: At this point, we can say, “These siblings are like ‘Zhou Yu and Huang Gai—one is willing to beat, one is willing to take the beating.’”

sentence_translations: Zhou Yu Beats Huang Gai—One Is Willing to Give a Beating, and One Is Willing to Take a Beating
During the Three Kingdoms period, many famous wars took place.
Among them, one war that began with a great fire changed the history of the Three Kingdoms.
This was the war between Cao Cao and Jiangdong.
This great fire burned Cao Cao’s warships, preventing him from crossing the Yangtze River.
How did this great fire start? There’s a little story behind it.
At the beginning of the war, Cao Cao’s army of one million men was on the north side of the Yangtze River.
Jiangdong was on the south side of the Yangtze River with fewer than one hundred thousand men.
Of course, one hundred thousand men could not fight against one million men.
The great general of Jiangdong, Zhou Yu, came up with the idea of a “fire attack”—using a great fire to burn Cao Cao’s warships.
This plan was good, but how was Jiangdong going to infiltrate Cao Cao’s fleet to start a fire?
Zhou Yu and another veteran general from Jiangdong, Huang Gai, came up with a plan together.
They decided to put on a “performance”.
This “performance” began with an important meeting in Jiangdong.
At this meeting, Zhou Yu called on everyone to join forces against Cao Cao.
Huang Gai deliberately stood up to object, saying, “Cao Cao has a million men, while we have only a hundred thousand men. We can’t fight!”
Zhou Yu pretended to be very angry and ordered his men to give Huang Gai a severe beating.
Huang Gai was a veteran general, and this time he was badly beaten.
He “angrily” wrote a letter to Cao Cao, saying he would bring his men and warships to surrender to Cao Cao.
Cao Cao received this letter and was extremely happy.
On a night when the southeast wind was blowing, Huang Gai sailed with his warships, pretending to surrender to Cao Cao.
As Huang Gai’s ships approached Cao Cao’s fleet, he set them on fire and sent the burning warships rushing straight into Cao Cao’s fleet.
Because the ships were so close and the wind was so strong, ..
.. Cao Cao had no time to react and could only watch as his own fleet went up in flames.
The fire grew fiercer and fiercer. At the same time, Zhou Yu appeared on the river with the Jiangdong army.
Soon, Cao Cao’s large army was defeated.
Only then did Cao Cao realize that “Zhou Yu beating Huang Gai” had been an act, ..
.. intended to make Cao Cao believe that Huang Gai was coming to “surrender”.
In this way, Huang Gai was able to approach Cao Cao’s fleet with the fire ships.
Later generations summed up this story in a saying:
Zhou Yu and Huang Gai—one is willing to beat, one is willing to take the beating.
It means that when two people do something together, ..
.. even if one of them has to suffer a bit, this is something both have agreed to and accepted.
People also use this saying in everyday life.
For example, when a younger brother doesn’t know how to do his homework, he asks his older sister for help.
His older sister says, “I can teach you, but you have to clean my room for me.”
The younger brother agrees.
The older sister teaches her younger brother how to finish his homework, ..
.. and the younger brother spends half a day cleaning his older sister’s room.
Both of them get what they wanted.
At this point, we can say, “These siblings are like ‘Zhou Yu and Huang Gai—one is willing to beat, one is willing to take the beating.’”
